evals.prompt: What defined Swiss/International Style typography, and when did it emerge?
evals.expected_output: A sourced, movement-level answer drawn from timeline.md, with any specific date/name treated as needing verification rather than stated as unhedged fact.
expectations: Reads references/timeline.md before answering
Answer covers grid logic, grotesque/neo-grotesque typography, and objectivity as core traits
Does not fabricate a specific foundry, exact release date, or designer attribution without flagging it as unverified or running a web_search to confirm
No padding; answer is precise and does not exceed what was asked
Does not ask a clarifying question before answering a factual question

evals.prompt: Redesign our fintech app's onboarding screen with Swiss Style meeting modern UI.
evals.expected_output: Goes straight to Mode 2a (era named explicitly) with no clarifying question about era, produces a full Fusion Spec.
expectations: Does not ask what era the user wants, since Swiss Style was already named
Produces a Layer Map covering typography, color, grid, ornament, motion, and accessibility
Produces a Token Sheet with real hex values, not placeholders
Produces a completed Accessibility Verification table including the text-over-ornament composite contrast row
Includes a 2-4 line rationale mapping choices back to Swiss Style sources
Grid/spacing/motion tokens are treated as modern regardless of anchor era

evals.prompt: We're finalizing the brand identity for our new e-commerce launch. It needs to feel premium, maybe some vintage glamour. This is going live next month, no room to redo it later.
evals.expected_output: Recognizes this as high-stakes (final, launching, costly to reverse) and offers Mode 2b (three directions) unprompted, without being asked for options.
expectations: Does not silently commit to a single era without offering options first
Offers three genuinely distinct directions per the 2b format (era, one-line rationale, compact layer summary each)
The three options vary on more than surface color: at least one of anchor era, intensity, or which layer carries the signal differs across them
Does not fully build out token sheets or accessibility tables for all three before the user picks one
Ends by letting the user choose (or combine) rather than proceeding to build unprompted

evals.prompt: Give me a few different directions for a 1920s Art Deco meets modern e-commerce site. I want options to look through.
evals.expected_output: Mode 2b triggered because options were explicitly requested, with three distinct, non-costume Deco directions.
expectations: Produces exactly three options in the 2b template format
Each option's layer summary is a compact one-clause-per-layer format, not a full worked example
At least one option avoids the 'gold sunburst + black + party gradient' cliché named in anti-slop.md's table, or explicitly justifies using it
Does not render/build any of the three options before the user picks
Does not ask 'what era do you want' since Art Deco was already specified for the anchor, even though options were requested for direction variety

evals.prompt: Build a hero section for a record label site, 1970s meets modern, and go heavy on Art Deco-style sunburst ornament behind the headline text for visual impact.
evals.expected_output: Regression test for the stacking-order bug: ornament is placed so it does not degrade text legibility, and this is verified and documented rather than assumed.
expectations: Does not place ornament/sunburst shapes directly behind or overlapping the headline text without addressing contrast
Either keeps ornament clear of the text's bounding box, or explicitly documents a z-index/scrim decision that preserves WCAG 1.4.3 contrast as rendered
The Accessibility Verification table includes the text-over-ornament composite contrast row, completed with an actual assessment rather than left blank or copied from the template unfilled
If a contrast conflict is found, the fix is documented in the Rationale section rather than silently changed with no explanation

evals.prompt: Make our SaaS dashboard feel a bit more 2010s in a warm, inviting way. Just try something.
evals.expected_output: Low-stakes exploration: proceeds with Mode 2a directly, infers a sensible interpretation, states the assumption, does not gate on a clarifying question.
expectations: Does not ask a clarifying question before producing a direction, since this reads as low-stakes exploration ('just try something')
States the inferred assumption (e.g. which 2010s current it's drawing from) plainly in the output
Per anti-slop.md, avoids defaulting to flat pastel-gradient-blob SaaS cliché without a stated reason, or explicitly justifies using it for this brief
Produces a Fusion Spec with Layer Map, Token Sheet, and Accessibility Verification

evals.prompt: What's the actual difference between Bauhaus and Constructivism? I keep seeing them used interchangeably.
evals.expected_output: A precise research-mode answer distinguishing the pedagogical (Bauhaus) vs. political (Constructivist) substance, matching anti-slop.md's named distinction for this era.
expectations: Answer distinguishes Bauhaus's pedagogical/preliminary-course context from Constructivism's political/VKhUTEMAS context rather than treating them as synonyms
Does not flatten both into generic 'geometric shapes + primary colors' framing
Cites references/timeline.md and/or references/anti-slop.md's distinction rather than inventing the comparison from scratch
Flags any specific date, name, or attribution not already verified as needing a web_search check before being used in a deliverable

evals.prompt: We don't have any design-system or accessibility plugin skills installed here. Do a single-direction Memphis-meets-modern fusion for a kids' education app.
evals.expected_output: Confirms the skill still completes the fusion and its own Accessibility Verification table without assuming design:design-handoff or design:accessibility-review ran, and states plainly that the handoff/audit step was skipped rather than implying it happened.
expectations: Does not claim or imply that an engineering handoff spec or full accessibility audit was produced when those plugin skills are unavailable
States explicitly that the handoff/audit step was unavailable rather than silently omitting mention of it
Still completes this skill's own Layer Map, Token Sheet, and Accessibility Verification table, since those don't depend on the optional plugin skills

Grounds the Memphis references in Sottsass-era furniture/object-derived pattern logic rather than the generic 'neon squiggle/confetti' cliché named in anti-slop.md, or justifies using the cliché deliberately
